stages.title: Power-button request
stages.headline: A switch event, not fingerprint authentication.
stages.explanation: A press requests normal startup. The same cap houses Touch ID, but pressing it is distinct from authenticating a fingerprint.
stages.observable: The button is highlighted; its functional connection leads to the logic-board control domain.
stages.known: Apple documents press-and-release startup and the Touch ID flex connection.
stages.unknown: The switch net name, pin assignment and receiving circuit are not verified here.

stages.title: Energy & regulated supply
stages.headline: The system uses available electrical energy.
stages.explanation: The battery or an attached adapter provides energy. Regulation supplies the electronics. The amber overlay shows a functional feed and return, not a measured current waveform.
stages.observable: Battery, management region and system supply relationship illuminate.
stages.known: Published battery capacity and supported charging inputs; battery connection to the board.
stages.unknown: Base-M4 rail voltages, PMIC identity, enable timing and PCB current paths are not established. This is a general electrical principle, not an exact rail sequence.

stages.title: Boot ROM → LLB
stages.headline: Immutable code starts the chain of trust.
stages.explanation: Apple silicon starts with Boot ROM code. It checks the signature of the low-level bootloader before that stage runs.
stages.observable: The ROM-to-LLB verification link is shown in the logical M4 inset.
stages.known: The platform boot chain and signature check are published by Apple.
stages.unknown: No physical ROM floorplan or board-level transfer trace is claimed.

stages.title: LLB & paired firmware
stages.headline: Controllers receive verified firmware.
stages.explanation: LLB checks system-paired firmware for chip controllers, including storage and display functions. This is an early boot responsibility, not proof that every peripheral is initialized in a serial order.
stages.observable: Controller domains illuminate inside the chip inset.
stages.known: LLB responsibilities are described in Apple Platform Security.
stages.unknown: Exact controller timing, bus transactions and base-M4 package routing are not public in the references used.

stages.title: LocalPolicy & Secure Enclave
stages.headline: The chosen security policy is verified.
stages.explanation: LLB verifies the Secure Enclave signed LocalPolicy and checks its anti-replay value against secure storage. This is a policy check; user fingerprint data does not flow through the power button to boot macOS.
stages.observable: The policy, Secure Enclave and secure-storage relationships are marked.
stages.known: Apple documents policy signing and anti-replay validation.
stages.unknown: The inset is a logical diagram. It does not locate secure-storage circuitry on this board.

stages.title: Policy-controlled iBoot verification
stages.headline: The next loader must satisfy the policy.
stages.explanation: LLB evaluates the iBoot signature according to LocalPolicy. This demonstration follows the Full Security path. The failure experiment stops this path and shows recovery instead.
stages.observable: A verification gate joins LLB to iBoot.
stages.known: The policy-dependent check and recovery behavior are documented.
stages.unknown: Verification duration is illustrative. No cryptographic operations run against real firmware here.

stages.title: Boot data → unified memory
stages.headline: Stored bytes become executable boot state.
stages.explanation: iBoot loads the device tree, trust cache and Boot Kernel Collection. An Auxiliary Kernel Collection is conditional on policy. The cyan paths distinguish storage reads from memory writes.
stages.observable: Storage, the M4 controller domain and the unified-memory relationship light up.
stages.known: Apple lists these loaded objects; unified memory is a published M4 feature.
stages.unknown: Package placement, exact transfer order, DMA details and physical memory traces are not verified. Memory is already usable here; this is not a claim about first DRAM initialization.

stages.title: Signed system volume integrity
stages.headline: The system volume must pass its integrity check.
stages.explanation: iBoot verifies the signed system volume root hash when required by policy. The line represents an integrity relationship, not a current flowing through NAND cells.
stages.observable: A violet verification marker joins the boot verifier and storage domain.
stages.known: The SSV root-hash check is part of the documented startup path.
stages.unknown: The diagram does not reproduce storage encryption keys, flash layout or a live filesystem scan.

stages.title: Handoff to the kernel
stages.headline: Verified boot state passes to the operating system.
stages.explanation: The loader hands execution to the OS kernel. The kernel takes over initialization and system operation. Many activities overlap; this timeline presents responsibilities as readable stages.
stages.observable: The kernel and shared-memory domains remain active.
stages.known: Kernel handoff is described in independent Apple-silicon platform research.
stages.unknown: The scene does not reproduce XNU execution, scheduling, device-driver traffic or per-core activity.

stages.title: Startup reaches a login boundary
stages.headline: A visible interface is the result—not the boot mechanism.
stages.explanation: The screen shows an illustrative login boundary. Authentication and FileVault can change the visible sequence; no credentials are collected and no automatic login is assumed.
stages.observable: The display data relationship is highlighted and the simulated screen changes.
stages.known: Apple documents startup login screens and FileVault-dependent authentication.
stages.unknown: Screen timing is illustrative. It is not a captured boot or a universal ordering of the login UI.
